85397.q: Which living things are especially good at breaking down dead wood in the forest?
85397.e: Fungi grow into dead wood and slowly make it soft and rotten. Over time it becomes new forest soil.

85398.q: What does the screen at the entrance to the treatment plant hold back?
85398.e: The screen is a grid with narrow bars. It catches large things such as rags, sticks and branches.
85398.m: The screen fishes large things out of the waste water.

85399.q: Why should a compost heap not dry out completely?
85399.e: Worms, fungi and bacteria can only work if it is damp enough. Good compost is as damp as a squeezed-out sponge.

85400.q: What can you make from an old bike inner tube?
85400.e: A bike inner tube is made of rubber and is very tough. You can make belts, purses or bags from it.
85400.m: You can make belts from bike inner tubes.

85501.q: Which distance on a pair of compasses is equal to the radius of the circle you draw?
a: The distance from the point to the pencil lead
The length of one compass arm
The height of the compass handle
85501.e: The point stays at the centre while the lead draws the circle. So the distance between them is exactly the radius.
85501.m: The opening of the compasses is always the radius of the circle.

85502.q: You want to draw a circle with a diameter of 10 cm using a pair of compasses. How wide do you open the compasses?
85502.e: The radius is half the diameter: 10 cm ÷ 2 is 5 cm.
85502.m: To draw a circle, open the compasses to half the diameter.

85503.q: How many times can you mark off the radius of a circle exactly around the circle with a pair of compasses?
85503.e: The chord and radius form equilateral triangles with the centre, with angles of 60°. As 360° ÷ 60° is 6, the radius fits exactly 6 times.
85503.m: If you mark off the radius six times around a circle, you get a regular hexagon.

85504.q: Which triangle is especially easy to construct from a line segment using only compasses and a ruler?
85504.e: You draw a circle around each end point with the length of the segment as the radius. Where they cross is the third corner.
85504.m: Two circles with the side length as radius give the top of the equilateral triangle.

85505.q: Apart from drawing circles, what else are compasses often used for?
85505.e: With compasses you can take a length and mark it off exactly the same somewhere else.
85505.m: Compasses let you copy lengths accurately.

85506.q: Which famous task has been proven impossible using only compasses and a ruler?
85506.e: You cannot construct a square with exactly the same area as a given circle. This was proven in 1882 by Ferdinand von Lindemann.
85506.m: Squaring the circle can never be done with compasses and a ruler.

85507.q: A circle has a radius of 4 cm. How long is its diameter?
85507.e: The diameter is twice as long as the radius: 2 times 4 cm is 8 cm.
85507.m: The diameter is always twice as long as the radius.

85508.q: What do you call the set of all points that are exactly 3 cm away from a point M?
a: A circle around M with radius 3 cm
A square around M with side 3 cm
A 3 cm line segment through M
85508.e: That is exactly what compasses draw: all points at the same distance from the centre.
85508.m: All points at the same distance from a centre form a circle.

85509.q: What shape is a set square with a protractor scale (a geometry triangle)?
85509.e: The geometry triangle has a right angle and two sides of equal length next to this angle.
85509.m: The geometry triangle is an isosceles right-angled triangle.

85510.q: How big are the two acute angles of a geometry triangle (set square)?
85510.e: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. After the right angle, 90° are left, shared equally between two angles.
85510.m: A geometry triangle has one right angle and two angles of 45°.

85511.q: Where is the zero of the centimetre scale on a geometry triangle (set square)?
a: In the middle of the long side
85511.e: The scale runs from the middle to the left and right. So you can measure in both directions from one point.
85511.m: On a geometry triangle, the centimetre scale starts in the middle.

85512.q: What is the centre line running from the zero point to the tip of a geometry triangle for?
85512.e: The line is at right angles to the long side. If you place it on a line, you can draw a perpendicular along the long side.
85512.m: You use the centre line of the geometry triangle to draw right angles.

85513.q: How many degrees does the angle scale on a geometry triangle cover?
85513.e: The angle scale is a semicircle. It goes from 0° to 180° and is usually labelled in both directions.
85513.m: The angle scale of the geometry triangle goes up to 180°.

85514.q: What are the thin lines printed parallel to the long side of a geometry triangle for?
85514.e: If you place one of these lines on a straight line, the long edge is parallel to it. This way you draw parallel lines at a set distance.
85514.m: The printed guide lines help you draw parallel lines.

85515.q: Why does the angle scale on a geometry triangle usually have two rows of numbers?
a: You can measure from the left and from the right
85515.e: One row counts from the left, the other from the right. You choose the row that starts at 0° on the arm of the angle.
85515.m: When measuring an angle, read the scale that starts at 0° on the first arm.

85516.q: You measure an angle with a geometry triangle and read 130°. What kind of angle is it?
85516.e: An angle between 90° and 180° is called obtuse. 130° is in this range.
85516.m: Angles between 90° and 180° are called obtuse.

85517.q: What is the perpendicular bisector of a line segment?
a: The perpendicular through the midpoint of the segment
The parallel line through one end point
The perpendicular through one end point
85517.e: The perpendicular bisector goes through the middle of the segment and is at right angles to it.
85517.m: The perpendicular bisector cuts a segment in half at a right angle.

85518.q: What do all points on the perpendicular bisector of the segment AB have in common?
a: They are the same distance from A and B
They all lie on the segment AB
They are closer to A than to B
They are the same distance from AB and A
85518.e: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from both end points. That is why it is used for “equally far away” problems.
85518.m: On the perpendicular bisector, you are equally far from both end points.

85519.q: How do you construct the perpendicular bisector without measuring?
a: With two arcs of the same size
85519.e: You draw arcs with the same radius around A and around B. The line through the two points where they cross is the perpendicular bisector.
85519.m: Two equal arcs around the end points give the perpendicular bisector.

85520.q: The segment AB is 6 cm long. Which compass radius is NOT enough to construct the perpendicular bisector?
85520.e: The radius must be more than half the segment, so more than 3 cm here. With 2 cm the arcs do not cross.
85520.m: For the perpendicular bisector, the compass radius must be more than half the segment.

85521.q: The segment AB is 9 cm long. Its perpendicular bisector crosses AB at point M. How far is M from A?
85521.e: The perpendicular bisector goes through the middle of the segment. 9 cm ÷ 2 is 4.5 cm.
85521.m: The perpendicular bisector meets the segment exactly in its middle.

85522.q: What is the smallest number of perpendicular bisectors you need to draw to find the centre of a triangle's circumcircle?
85522.e: Two perpendicular bisectors already cross at one point. The third one automatically goes through this point too.
85522.m: Two perpendicular bisectors are enough; the third is only a check.

85523.q: A point P is reflected in a line g, giving P'. What is g for the segment PP'?
85523.e: In a reflection, the mirror line is at right angles to PP' and cuts it in half. That is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
85523.m: The mirror line is the perpendicular bisector between a point and its image.

85524.q: How many perpendicular bisectors can you draw in a triangle?
85524.e: Each of the three sides has its own perpendicular bisector.
85524.m: A triangle has three sides and so three perpendicular bisectors.

85525.q: What does an angle bisector do?
a: It divides an angle into two equal parts
It is perpendicular to an arm
85525.e: The angle bisector is a ray from the vertex that divides the angle into two equal angles.
85525.m: The angle bisector divides an angle into two equal halves.

85526.q: An angle measures 74°. How big are the two angles made by the angle bisector?
85526.e: The angle bisector divides it into two equal parts: 74° ÷ 2 is 37°.
85526.m: If you halve an angle, each half is half as big.

85527.q: What do all points on an angle bisector have in common?
a: The same distance from both arms
The same distance from the vertex
The same distance from two points
85527.e: Every point on the angle bisector is equally far from both arms, measured at right angles to the arm.
85527.m: On the angle bisector, you are equally far from both arms.

85528.q: What is the first step in constructing an angle bisector with compasses and a ruler?
a: A line parallel to one arm
85528.e: The arc around the vertex crosses both arms. Around these points you draw arcs of equal size; where they cross lies on the bisector.
85528.m: You construct the angle bisector with arcs, without measuring.

85529.q: What is the angle bisector for the two arms of an angle?
85529.e: If you reflect one arm in the angle bisector, it lands exactly on the other arm.
85529.m: An angle is symmetrical about its angle bisector.

85530.q: Two adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180°. What angle do their two angle bisectors make?
85530.e: Each bisector takes half of its angle. Together that is half of 180°, so 90°.
85530.m: The angle bisectors of adjacent angles on a straight line are at right angles to each other.

85531.q: How many bisectors of interior angles does a triangle have?
85531.e: A triangle has three interior angles, and each one has its own angle bisector.
85531.m: Each of the three angles of a triangle has its own angle bisector.

85532.q: In a square, what is the angle bisector of a corner angle?
85532.e: The diagonal of the square divides the right angle at the corner into two angles of 45°.
85532.m: In a square, the diagonals halve the corner angles.

85533.q: What is the incircle of a triangle?
a: A circle that touches all three sides from inside
A circle through all three corners
A circle around the midpoint of the longest side
A circle with the perimeter as its radius
85533.e: The incircle lies inside the triangle and touches each side at exactly one point.
85533.m: The incircle touches all sides of a triangle from inside.

85534.q: Which lines meet at the centre of the incircle?
85534.e: The centre of the incircle must be the same distance from all three sides. Exactly the points on the angle bisectors do that.
85534.m: You find the centre of the incircle with the angle bisectors.

85535.q: Where is the centre of a triangle's incircle?
85535.e: As the incircle lies completely inside the triangle, its centre is also inside in every triangle.
85535.m: The centre of the incircle is inside every triangle.

85536.q: Once you have found the centre, how do you find the radius of the incircle?
a: The perpendicular distance to a side
Half the length of the longest side
The distance to the midpoint of a side
85536.e: The radius is the shortest distance from the centre to a side. To find it, you draw a perpendicular onto a side.
85536.m: You get the incircle radius with the perpendicular from the centre to a side.

85537.q: A square has sides of 8 cm. How big is the radius of its incircle?
85537.e: The incircle touches two opposite sides. So its diameter is 8 cm and its radius 4 cm.
85537.m: In a square, the incircle radius is half the side length.

85538.q: Which of these quadrilaterals always has an incircle?
85538.e: In a rhombus all sides are the same length, and the diagonals halve the angles. Where they cross is the centre of the incircle.
85538.m: A rhombus always has an incircle.

85539.q: What are the sides of a triangle called in relation to its incircle?
85539.e: A straight line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a tangent.
85539.m: Each side of a triangle is a tangent to its incircle.

85540.q: What is a quadrilateral that has an incircle called?
85540.e: Because all four sides touch the incircle, so they are tangents, it is called a tangential quadrilateral.
85540.m: A quadrilateral with an incircle is called a tangential quadrilateral.

85541.q: What is the circumcircle of a triangle?
a: A circle through all three corners
A circle that touches all sides from inside
A circle around a single corner
A circle with the longest side as radius
85541.e: The circumcircle goes through all three corners and surrounds the triangle.
85541.m: The circumcircle of a triangle goes through all three corners.

85542.q: Which lines meet at the centre of the circumcircle?
85542.e: The centre of the circumcircle is equally far from all three corners. That is true for the point where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
85542.m: You find the centre of the circumcircle with the perpendicular bisectors.

85543.q: Where is the centre of the circumcircle of an obtuse triangle?
85543.e: In an obtuse triangle, the perpendicular bisectors meet beyond the longest side, so outside.
85543.m: In obtuse triangles, the centre of the circumcircle is outside.

85544.q: Where is the centre of the circumcircle of an acute triangle?
85544.e: If all angles are smaller than 90°, the perpendicular bisectors meet inside the triangle.
85544.m: In acute triangles, the centre of the circumcircle is inside.

85545.q: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 8 cm wide. How big is the radius of its circumcircle?
85545.e: The diagonal is a diameter: the square root of (36 + 64) is 10 cm. The radius is half of that, so 5 cm.
85545.m: In a rectangle, the circumcircle radius is half the diagonal.

85546.q: In which quadrilateral do all four corners always lie on one shared circle?
85546.e: In a rectangle, the diagonals are the same length and cut each other in half. So the point where they cross is equally far from all four corners and is the centre of the circumcircle.
85546.m: Every rectangle has a circumcircle through all four corners.

85547.q: In an equilateral triangle, which centre is in the same place as the centre of the circumcircle?
85547.e: In an equilateral triangle, the perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors are the same lines. So both centres are at the same point.
85547.m: In an equilateral triangle, the incircle and circumcircle have the same centre.

85548.q: How many circles go through three points that do not lie on a straight line?
85548.e: The three points form a triangle. There is exactly one circumcircle, and its centre is where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
85548.m: Exactly one circle goes through three points not on a straight line.

85549.q: At what angle are the edges going backwards usually drawn in a school oblique drawing?
85549.e: The usual angle is 45° to the horizontal front edge. This creates a 3D effect.
85549.m: In an oblique drawing, depth is often drawn at 45°.

85550.q: How long are the edges going backwards drawn in the usual school oblique drawing?
85550.e: The depth edges are shortened to half so that the solid does not look too long.
85550.m: In an oblique drawing, depth edges are usually shortened to half.

85551.q: A cube has edges of 4 cm. In an oblique drawing with depth shortened to half, how long do you draw the depth edges?
85551.e: The depth edges are halved: 4 cm ÷ 2 is 2 cm. The front face stays 4 cm by 4 cm.
85551.m: Only depth is shortened in an oblique drawing; the front face stays the same.

85552.q: How do you draw edges that cannot actually be seen in an oblique drawing?
85552.e: Hidden edges are drawn as dashed lines. That way the solid stays easy to recognise.
85552.m: Hidden edges are drawn dashed in an oblique drawing.

85553.q: Which face of a cuboid appears at its true size in an oblique drawing?
85553.e: The front face is drawn unchanged. Only the edges going backwards are slanted and shortened.
85553.m: In an oblique drawing, the front face is not distorted.

85554.q: In an oblique drawing, what happens to edges that are parallel on the solid?
85554.e: An oblique drawing is a parallel projection. So parallel edges are shown as parallel again.
85554.m: In an oblique drawing, parallel edges stay parallel.

85555.q: What does the square top face of a cube look like in an oblique drawing?
85555.e: Two sides are horizontal and the same length, the other two are slanted and shortened. This makes a parallelogram.
85555.m: In an oblique drawing, the top face of a cube becomes a parallelogram.

85556.q: How many edges of a cube are hidden, and so dashed, in the usual oblique drawing?
85556.e: Three edges you cannot see come out of the bottom back corner. The other 9 edges are visible.
85556.m: In an oblique drawing of a cube, three edges are hidden.

85557.q: From which direction do you see a solid in a plan view?
85557.e: The plan view is the view from above, like the floor plan of a flat.
85557.m: The plan view shows a solid from above.

85558.q: From which direction do you see a solid in a front elevation?
85558.e: The front elevation is the view of a solid from the front.
85558.m: The front elevation shows a solid from the front.

85559.q: What is the view of a solid from the side called?
85559.e: As well as the plan view (above) and front elevation (front), there is the side elevation for the view from the left or right.
85559.m: The side view of a solid is called the side elevation.

85560.q: A cylinder is standing upright. What does its front elevation look like?
85560.e: From the front you see the width (diameter) and the height, so a rectangle.
85560.m: A standing cylinder looks like a rectangle from the front.

85561.q: A cone is standing on its base. What does its front elevation look like?
85561.e: From the front you see the base as a line with the tip above it. This makes a triangle.
85561.m: A standing cone looks like a triangle from the front.

85562.q: Which solid always looks like a circle in the plan view, front elevation and side elevation?
85562.e: A sphere looks the same from every direction, namely like a circle.
85562.m: A sphere looks like a circle in every view.

85563.q: A pyramid with a square base is standing upright. What does its plan view look like?
a: A triangle with a centre line
A circle with a centre point
85563.e: From above you see the square of the base. The edges up to the tip look like lines from the corners to the middle, just like the diagonals.
85563.m: From above, a square pyramid looks like a square with diagonals.

85564.q: Where are plan views and elevations used especially often in everyday life?
85564.e: Architects and builders draw houses from above and from the front. That way the building can be built exactly.
85564.m: Building plans show houses in plan view and elevation.

85565.q: What is the formula for the surface area of a cube with edge a?
85565.e: A cube has 6 square faces of the same size, each a times a.
85565.m: The surface area of a cube is made of six equal squares.

85566.q: What is the surface area of a cube with edges of 5 cm?
85566.e: One face is 5 times 5 = 25 cm². Six faces make 6 times 25 = 150 cm².
85566.m: For the surface of a cube, multiply one face by six.

85567.q: What is the surface area of a cuboid with edges of 5 cm, 4 cm and 3 cm?
85567.e: The three different faces are 20, 15 and 12 cm². Together that is 47 cm², and doubled it is 94 cm².
85567.m: In a cuboid, each face appears twice.

85568.q: In which unit do you give a surface area if the edges are measured in cm?
85568.e: A surface is an area. Areas are measured in square units such as cm².
85568.m: Surface areas are given in square centimetres or other units of area.

85569.q: What happens to the surface area of a cube if you double all the edges?
85569.e: Each face becomes 2 times 2 = 4 times as big. So the whole surface also becomes four times as big.
85569.m: If you double the edges, the surface area becomes four times as big.

85570.q: What is the curved surface between the top and bottom of a cylinder called?
85570.e: Unrolled, the curved surface is a rectangle. It is as long as the circumference of the circle and as high as the cylinder.
85570.m: The curved side of a cylinder is called its lateral surface.

85571.q: A box is 10 cm long, 10 cm wide and 5 cm high. What is the least amount of paper you need to cover it without overlaps?
85571.e: Bottom and lid: 2 times 100 = 200 cm². Four sides: 4 times 50 = 200 cm². Together 400 cm².
85571.m: To cover a box you need as much paper as its surface area.

85572.q: A pyramid has a square base with sides of 6 cm. Each side triangle has a height of 5 cm. What is its surface area?
85572.e: Base: 6 times 6 = 36 cm². One triangle: 6 times 5 ÷ 2 = 15 cm², four of them make 60 cm². Together 96 cm².
85572.m: The surface of a pyramid is the base plus all the side triangles.

85573.q: What especially helps when calculating surface area, because you can see all the faces side by side?
85573.e: In a net, all faces are spread out flat. You calculate each face and add them up.
85573.m: A net shows all the faces that make up the surface.

85574.q: How many Platonic solids are there?
85574.e: There are exactly five: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron.
85574.m: There are exactly five Platonic solids.

85575.q: The Platonic solids are named after Plato. Who was Plato?
85575.e: Plato was a Greek philosopher who lived in Athens about 2,400 years ago. He described these solids in his work “Timaeus”.
85575.m: The Platonic solids are named after the Greek philosopher Plato.

85576.q: What faces make up a dodecahedron?
85576.e: The dodecahedron has 12 regular pentagons as faces. “Dodeka” means twelve.
85576.m: A dodecahedron has twelve pentagonal faces.

85577.q: How many equilateral triangles make up an icosahedron?
85577.e: “Eikosi” means twenty in Greek. The icosahedron has 20 equilateral triangles.
85577.m: The icosahedron is made of twenty triangles.

85578.q: Which Platonic solid is made of 8 equilateral triangles?
85578.e: “Okto” means eight. The octahedron looks like two pyramids joined at their square bases.
85578.m: The octahedron has eight triangular faces.

85579.q: Which Platonic solid has the fewest faces?
85579.e: The tetrahedron has only 4 faces. It is a pyramid made of four equilateral triangles.
85579.m: The tetrahedron is the Platonic solid with only four faces.

85580.q: By what other name is the cube known as a Platonic solid?
85580.e: “Hexa” means six. The cube has 6 faces and so is also called a hexahedron.
85580.m: As a Platonic solid, the cube is also called a hexahedron.

85581.q: What condition must the faces of a Platonic solid meet?
85581.e: All faces are identical regular polygons, and the same number of faces meet at every corner.
85581.m: Platonic solids are made only of identical regular polygons.

85582.q: Why is there no Platonic solid made of regular hexagons?
a: Three hexagons at a corner lie flat
85582.e: The angle of a hexagon is 120°. Three of them make 360°, so a flat surface without a corner.
85582.m: At a corner of a solid, the angles must add up to less than 360°.

85583.q: What does Euler's polyhedron formula say for vertices V, edges E and faces F?
a: V minus E plus F equals 2
V plus E plus F equals 2
85583.e: For every solid without holes and with flat faces: vertices minus edges plus faces is 2.
85583.m: For such solids, vertices minus edges plus faces always equals two.

85584.q: Which Swiss city did the mathematician Leonhard Euler come from?
85584.e: Leonhard Euler was born in Basel in 1707. He is considered one of the greatest mathematicians of all time.
85584.m: Leonhard Euler was a mathematician from Basel.

85585.q: Test the formula on a cube: what is 8 minus 12 plus 6?
85585.e: A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 faces. 8 minus 12 plus 6 is 2.
85585.m: For a cube too, vertices minus edges plus faces equals two.

85586.q: A solid has 12 vertices and 20 faces. How many edges does it have according to Euler's polyhedron formula?
85586.e: From 12 minus E plus 20 = 2 it follows that E = 30. This fits the icosahedron.
85586.m: You can use Euler's polyhedron formula to work out a missing number.

85587.q: A prism with a triangular base has 6 vertices and 5 faces. How many edges does it have?
85587.e: 6 minus E plus 5 = 2 gives E = 9: 3 edges each at the top and bottom and 3 upright ones.
85587.m: A triangular prism has nine edges.

85588.q: A pyramid has a pentagon as its base. How many edges does it have?
85588.e: It has 6 vertices and 6 faces. 6 minus E plus 6 = 2 gives E = 10.
85588.m: A pyramid has twice as many edges as its base has corners.

85589.q: A tetrahedron has 4 vertices and 4 faces. How many edges does it have?

85590.q: Which former Swiss banknote showed Leonhard Euler?
85590.e: Euler was shown on the 10-franc note of the Swiss National Bank's sixth series of banknotes, in circulation from 1979.
85590.m: Leonhard Euler once appeared on the Swiss 10-franc note.

85591.q: What does tessellation mean in geometry?
a: Covering a surface with no gaps or overlaps
85591.e: In a tessellation, a flat surface is completely covered with shapes, with no gaps and no overlaps.
85591.m: A tessellation covers a surface with no gaps and no overlaps.

85592.q: Which regular polygons can tessellate a flat surface on their own?
85592.e: Only for these three does the interior angle (60°, 90°, 120°) fit into 360° a whole number of times.
85592.m: Only triangles, squares and hexagons tessellate regularly on their own.

85593.q: What must the angles at a point in a tessellation add up to?
85593.e: Around a point there is a full angle of 360°, otherwise there are gaps or overlaps.
85593.m: At every corner point of a tessellation, the angles add up to 360°.

85594.q: Which regular polygons do you find in the honeycomb of a beehive?
85594.e: Honeycombs are made of hexagons. They fill the surface with no gaps.
85594.m: Honeycombs form a tessellation of hexagons.

85595.q: In a regular tessellation of triangles, how many equilateral triangles meet at one point?
85595.m: Six equilateral triangles fill a point in a tessellation.

85596.q: Why can you not make a gap-free tessellation with regular pentagons alone?
a: 108° does not fit into 360° a whole number of times
85596.e: Three pentagons make 324°, four already 432°. There is always a gap or an overlap.
85596.m: Regular pentagons always leave gaps when tessellating.

85597.q: Which floor is an example of a tessellation?
a: A floor of identical tiles with no gaps
A gravel path made of many little stones
85597.e: In a tessellation, a surface is covered with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps. A tiled floor is laid in exactly this way.

85598.q: Which combination of regular polygons is often used to lay a tiled floor?
85598.e: An octagon has interior angles of 135°. Two octagons and one square make 135° + 135° + 90° = 360°.
85598.m: Octagons and squares fit together into a gap-free tessellation.

85599.q: Which triangles can tessellate a flat surface with no gaps?
85599.e: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°. If you place each angle twice around a point, you get 360°.
85599.m: Every triangle can be used for tessellating.

85600.q: For which kind of solid does Euler's polyhedron formula with the result 2 not work?
a: Solids with a hole right through them
85600.e: For a solid with a hole, such as a square frame, vertices minus edges plus faces gives 0 instead of 2.
85600.m: The polyhedron formula with the result two only works for solids without a hole.

85601.q: What does a robot vacuum cleaner do?
a: It vacuums the floor on its own
85601.e: A robot vacuum cleaner drives through the flat on its own and sucks up dust and crumbs as it goes.
85601.m: A robot vacuum cleaner cleans the floor all on its own.

85602.q: Where does a robot vacuum cleaner go when its battery is almost empty?
85602.e: Many robot vacuum cleaners find their own way back to their charging station. There they charge their battery again.
85602.m: A robot vacuum cleaner gets new power at its charging station.

85603.q: Why does a good robot vacuum cleaner not fall down the stairs?
85603.e: It has sensors underneath. They notice when the floor suddenly stops, and the robot halts.
85603.m: Sensors protect the robot vacuum cleaner from falling.

85604.q: What should you tidy up off the floor before starting a robot vacuum cleaner?
85604.e: Small things like socks or cables can get caught in the brushes. Then the robot gets stuck.
85604.m: Before the robot vacuum runs, I clear small things off the floor.

85605.q: What does a robot vacuum cleaner notice when it bumps into a chair leg?
85605.e: A bumper with a sensor reports the touch. Then the robot turns away and carries on in another direction.
85605.m: The robot vacuum cleaner notices obstacles and drives around them.

85606.q: Where does a robot vacuum cleaner collect the dust?
85606.e: The dust ends up in a small container in the robot. You have to empty it regularly.
85606.m: You have to empty the robot vacuum's dust container often.

85607.q: What shape are many robot vacuum cleaners?
85607.e: Thanks to their flat round shape they fit under beds and sofas and turn easily.
85607.m: A flat robot vacuum cleaner can get under the sofa too.

85608.q: What spins at the front of many robot vacuum cleaners to get dust out of corners?
85608.e: Small side brushes sweep the dust out of corners and from edges towards the suction opening.
85608.m: With side brushes the robot vacuum gets dust out of the corners.

85609.q: What does a robotic lawnmower do?
85609.e: A robotic lawnmower drives over the lawn on its own and cuts the grass short.
85609.m: A robotic lawnmower cuts the lawn all on its own.

85610.q: How do many robotic lawnmowers know where the lawn ends?
a: From a wire in the ground
From the colour of the flowers
85610.e: Many robotic lawnmowers need a boundary wire around the edge of the lawn. It shows the robot the boundary.
85610.m: A wire in the ground shows the robotic lawnmower the boundary.

85611.q: Which animal is especially at risk from robotic lawnmowers at night?
85611.e: Hedgehogs are out and about at night and roll up when in danger instead of running away. That is why a robotic lawnmower should not run at night.
85611.m: A robotic lawnmower should rest at night to protect hedgehogs.

85612.q: What happens to the small bits of cut grass with a robotic lawnmower?
85612.e: The robot only cuts off small pieces. They stay where they fall and feed the lawn.
85612.m: The fine clippings from a robotic lawnmower feed the lawn.

85613.q: Why should small children not play on a robotic lawnmower while it is running?
85613.e: Sharp blades spin underneath the robotic lawnmower. You can hurt yourself on them.
85613.m: I keep my hands and feet away from a running robotic lawnmower.

85614.q: Where are the blades on a robotic lawnmower?
85614.e: The blades are under the casing, close to the grass. That way they cut off the blades of grass.
85614.m: The blades of a robotic lawnmower are underneath.

85615.q: What does a robotic lawnmower often do when it is raining heavily?
a: It goes into the charging station
85615.e: Many robotic lawnmowers have a rain sensor. When the grass is wet they wait in the station.
85615.m: In heavy rain the robotic lawnmower prefers to wait in its station.

85616.q: How often does a robotic lawnmower usually go over the lawn?
85616.e: Because it only cuts off a little, it runs often. That way the lawn always stays short.
85616.m: A robotic lawnmower mows often and only a little at a time.

85617.q: How do you give a voice assistant a task?
85617.e: A voice assistant understands spoken words. So you do not have to type anything.
85617.m: You control a voice assistant with your voice.

85618.q: What does a voice assistant use to hear what you say?
85618.e: The microphone picks up your voice. The computer then turns it into words.
85618.m: A voice assistant hears you with a microphone.

85619.q: What do you usually have to say first so that a voice assistant listens?
85619.e: A voice assistant waits for its wake word, which is often its own name. Only when it hears it does it accept the task.
85619.m: You wake up a voice assistant with its wake word.

85620.q: What can a voice assistant do for you, for example?
85620.e: It can set alarms, play music or tell you the weather. It cannot do jobs with hands.
85620.m: A voice assistant helps with words, not with hands.

85621.q: What helps a voice assistant understand you well?
85621.e: The computer can best recognise clear, distinct words.
85621.m: If you speak clearly, the voice assistant understands you better.

85622.q: Where do many voice assistants get their answers from?
a: From a book on the shelf
85622.e: The question is sent over the internet to computers. They look for an answer and send it back.
85622.m: Many voice assistants need the internet for their answers.

85623.q: Who do you ask before you let a voice assistant buy something?
a: A child you do not know
85623.e: A voice assistant can sometimes order things. That costs real money, so you ask your parents first.
85623.m: Before buying anything, I always ask my parents.

85624.q: Can a voice assistant give wrong answers too?
85624.e: A voice assistant can misunderstand a question or find wrong information. That is why you check important answers.
85624.m: Even a voice assistant sometimes makes mistakes.

85625.q: What does a motion sensor on a lamp do?
85625.e: When someone moves, the sensor notices and switches the lamp on.
85625.m: A motion sensor turns on the light when someone moves.

85626.q: What do many motion sensors detect?
85626.e: People and animals give off heat radiation. The sensor notices when this warmth moves.
85626.m: Many motion sensors detect the warmth of people and animals.

85627.q: With a lamp that has a motion sensor, what happens when nobody is there any more?
a: The light goes off after a while
The light stays on for ever
85627.e: After a set time without movement, the sensor switches the light off again.
85627.m: Without movement, the sensor switches the light off again.

85628.q: Why does a motion sensor save electricity?
a: The light is only on when needed
It does not need a lamp
85628.e: The light is only on when someone is there. That way it does not burn for nothing.
85628.m: A motion sensor helps to save electricity.

85629.q: Where do you often find a lamp with a motion sensor?
85629.e: In the stairwell or by the front door, the light comes on automatically like this.
85629.m: In the stairwell a motion sensor often switches on the light.

85630.q: You are sitting very still in the toilet and the light goes off. What helps?
85630.e: The motion sensor only reacts to movement. A movement switches the light back on.
85630.m: With a motion sensor, a movement helps against darkness.

85631.q: Apart from people, what can set off a motion sensor in the garden?
85631.e: A cat is warm and moves. That is why it can switch on the light too.
85631.m: Warm animals can set off a motion sensor too.

85632.q: What can a motion sensor in a burglar alarm set off?
85632.e: If someone moves in a protected room, the motion sensor reports it and the alarm goes off.
85632.m: Motion sensors also help in burglar alarms.

85633.q: What does a light sensor measure?
85633.e: A light sensor notices whether it is light or dark and how much light there is.

85634.q: When does a light sensor switch on a street lamp?
85634.e: When it gets dark in the evening, the sensor measures little light and switches on the lamp.
85634.m: Many street lamps come on at dusk with a light sensor.

85635.q: Why does a mobile phone have a light sensor?
85635.e: The sensor measures the light in the room. In the dark the screen gets dimmer, in the sun brighter.
85635.m: The light sensor in a phone adjusts the brightness of the screen.

85636.q: When does a solar lamp in the garden shine?
85636.e: During the day the sun charges the battery. A light sensor notices the darkness and switches the lamp on at night.
85636.m: A solar lamp charges during the day and shines at night.

85637.q: You hold your finger over a light sensor. What does it measure then?
85637.e: Your finger covers the sensor. Hardly any light gets in, so it measures dark.
85637.m: A covered light sensor reports darkness.

85638.q: A car drives into a tunnel. What can a light sensor in the car do then?
85638.e: In the tunnel it gets darker. The sensor notices and switches on the lights automatically.
85638.m: In a tunnel a light sensor switches on the car's lights.

85639.q: What can automatic blinds with a light sensor do when the sun is shining strongly?
85639.e: The sensor measures a lot of light. Then the blinds come down and the room stays cooler.
85639.m: A light sensor can control blinds in strong sunshine.

85640.q: How does a learning robot with light sensors recognise a black line on white paper?
a: Black is painted on more thickly
85640.e: White paper reflects a lot of light, a black line only a little. The sensor notices the difference.
85640.m: Light surfaces reflect more light than dark ones.

85641.q: How does a TV remote control often send its commands?
85641.e: Many remote controls send infrared light. Our eyes cannot see this light.
85641.m: Many remote controls send invisible infrared light.

85642.q: What can you do with a TV remote control, for example?
85642.e: With the buttons you change the channel, turn the sound up or down and switch it on and off.
85642.m: With the remote control you change the channel without getting up.

85643.q: What can sometimes make the light of an infrared remote control visible?
85643.e: Many cameras can see infrared light. On the screen the tip of the remote control then flashes.
85643.m: Some phone cameras show the infrared light of a remote control.

85644.q: What does a remote control need to work?
85644.e: The remote control needs electricity to send signals. It usually gets it from batteries.
85644.m: A remote control does not work without batteries.

85645.q: Why do you have to point an infrared remote control at the television?
a: The light must reach the receiver
So it does not fall down
85645.e: Infrared light travels in a straight line. It must reach the small receiver on the television.
85645.m: You aim an infrared remote control at the receiver.

85646.q: Does an infrared remote control work through a wall?
85646.e: Light does not go through a wall. That is why the remote control has to be in the same room.
85646.m: Infrared light does not get through walls.

85647.q: How is a remote-controlled toy car usually controlled?
85647.e: Radio waves also go through walls and reach further than infrared light. That is why many toy cars use radio.
85647.m: Remote-controlled toy cars are usually controlled by radio.

85648.q: Which door do people often open with a small remote control?
85648.e: A garage door with a motor receives the signal from a remote control and opens.
85648.m: Many garage doors are opened by remote control.

85649.q: How does an automatic door in a shop open?
85649.e: A sensor notices that someone is coming. Then a motor opens the door.
85649.m: An automatic door opens without being touched.

85650.q: What opens an automatic sliding door?
85650.e: An electric motor pushes the door panels to the side and back again.
85650.m: A motor moves an automatic door.

85651.q: Where is the sensor on many automatic doors?
a: At the top above the door
In the roof of the building
85651.e: Usually there is a small box above the door. It looks downwards and detects people.
85651.m: The door sensor is often above the door.

85652.q: What happens if someone is standing in the door while it closes?
85652.e: A sensor protects people. It notices that someone is in the way, and the door opens again.
85652.m: An automatic door does not trap people.

85653.q: What is an invisible beam that often notices whether someone is standing in a doorway called?
85653.e: A light barrier sends a beam of light across the doorway. If someone breaks the beam, the door notices.
85653.m: A light barrier notices when someone is blocking the doorway.

85654.q: Where do you often find automatic doors?
85654.e: Lots of people go in and out of shopping centres, stations and hospitals. Automatic doors help there.
85654.m: Where many people pass through, there are often automatic doors.

85655.q: Who do automatic doors help especially?
85655.e: Anyone in a wheelchair or carrying a lot can get through the door without touching it.
85655.m: Automatic doors make buildings easier for everyone to get into.

85656.q: Why should you not play with an automatic door?
85656.e: If you keep running back and forth, you could bump yourself or break the motor.
85656.m: You do not play with an automatic door.

85657.q: What do you buy at a ticket machine at the station?
85657.e: At the ticket machine you buy a ticket for the train, tram or bus.
85657.m: You buy a ticket at the ticket machine.

85658.q: How do you choose your destination on a modern ticket machine?
85658.e: Many machines have a touch-sensitive screen. You tap on the boxes with your finger.
85658.m: On a touchscreen you tap with your finger.

85659.q: What do you have to enter first at the ticket machine?
85659.e: The machine needs to know where the journey is going. Only then can it work out the price.
85659.m: At the ticket machine you choose the destination first.

85660.q: What can you pay with at many ticket machines?
85660.e: Many machines accept coins and payment cards.
85660.m: At the ticket machine you pay with money or a card.

85661.q: What does the machine give you back if you put in too much money?
85661.e: The machine works out how much too much was paid and gives back the rest as change.
85661.m: Money paid on top comes back as change.

85662.q: A ticket costs 4 francs. You put in 5 francs. How much change do you get?
85662.m: Change is the money put in minus the price.

85663.q: Up to which birthday do children travel free on trains in Switzerland?
85663.e: Children under 6 travel free in Switzerland, with or without an adult. After that they need a ticket (as of 2026).
85663.m: Children under 6 travel free on trains in Switzerland.

85664.q: How much do children aged 6 and over usually pay for a train ticket in Switzerland?
85664.e: Children aged 6 to 16 travel at half price. With a Junior Card they even travel free when with a parent (as of 2026).
85664.m: In Switzerland children usually travel by train at half price.

85665.q: What is a cash machine often called in Switzerland?
85665.e: In Switzerland people usually call a cash machine a Bancomat.
85665.m: In Switzerland a cash machine is often called a Bancomat.

85666.q: What do you get from a Bancomat?
85666.e: At a Bancomat you get money from your bank account in notes.
85666.m: You get cash from a Bancomat.

85667.q: What do you need to take money out of a Bancomat?
85667.e: You put in your bank card and type in the secret PIN code. That way the machine knows whose account it is.
85667.m: At a Bancomat you need a card and a PIN code.

85668.q: Who may you tell your PIN code to?
85668.e: The PIN is secret. Anyone who knows it can take money out with the card.
85668.m: You always keep your PIN code to yourself.

85669.q: What do you do when typing your PIN at a Bancomat?
a: Write it on a piece of paper
85669.e: That way nobody can see which numbers you are typing.
85669.m: When typing your PIN, you cover the keys with your hand.

85670.q: Where does the money you take out of a Bancomat come from?
a: It is a present from the machine
85670.e: The money is taken from your own account. So it is not a present.
85670.m: At a Bancomat you take money from your own account.

85671.q: What can happen if you type in the wrong PIN several times?
85671.e: For protection, the bank blocks the card after several wrong attempts.
85671.m: After several wrong PIN entries the card is blocked.

85672.q: What does a Bancomat usually give back first?
85672.e: Many machines give the card back first and only then the money. That way you do not forget the card.
85672.m: At a Bancomat you take your card back first.

a: A car that drives by itself
85673.e: A computer in the car steers, brakes and accelerates. A person does not have to drive.
85673.m: A self-driving car is controlled by a computer.

85674.q: What does a self-driving car use to see the road?
85674.e: Cameras, radar and other sensors all around the car pick up the road, cars and people.
85674.m: A self-driving car sees with cameras and sensors.

85675.q: Why does a person often still ride along in tests with self-driving buses?
a: So they can stop the bus
So they can clean the roads
85675.e: In tests a person often rides along. They can stop the bus if something unexpected happens.
85675.m: In tests with self-driving buses a person often keeps watch.

85676.q: What must a self-driving car be able to recognise in every case?
85676.e: For safety, the car must see pedestrians and cyclists early so it can brake.
85676.m: A self-driving car must reliably recognise people.

85677.q: What helps a self-driving car find its way?
85677.e: With a digital map and satellite positioning, the car knows where it is and where it has to go.
85677.m: A self-driving car finds its way with a digital map.

85678.q: What can make things difficult for the cameras of a self-driving car?
85678.e: In fog, snow or heavy rain, cameras cannot see well. Then driving is harder.
85678.m: Bad weather makes things hard for self-driving cars.

85679.q: What did PostBus test in Sion from 2016 with real passengers?
85679.e: PostBus tested small self-driving buses with passengers in Sion in the Valais. They ran without a driver, but an attendant was on board.
85679.m: Self-driving PostBus buses ran early on in Sion.

85680.q: What does a self-driving car do at a red traffic light?
85680.e: A computer has to follow the traffic rules too. At red it stops.
85680.m: A self-driving car stops at red too.

85681.q: What makes a toy drone fly?
85681.e: Spinning propellers push air downwards. That makes the drone rise.
85681.m: A drone flies with spinning propellers.

85682.q: How many propellers does a typical toy drone have?
85682.e: Most small drones are quadcopters. “Quad” means four.

85683.q: What do you use to steer a toy drone?
85683.e: You steer the drone with a remote control or an app. The commands are sent by radio.
85683.m: A drone is steered with a remote control.

85684.q: Where does a toy drone get its power from?
85684.e: A small battery supplies the power for the motors. It usually only lasts a few minutes.
85684.m: A toy drone's battery only lasts a short time.

85685.q: Where must you not fly a drone?
a: In your own garden with nobody there
85685.e: A drone could crash and hurt people. That is why you never fly over lots of people.
85685.m: I never fly a drone over crowds.

85686.q: What must you always do when flying a drone?
a: Be able to see the drone
85686.e: You must always be able to see the drone with your own eyes so you can steer it safely.
85686.m: When flying a drone, I always keep it in sight.

85687.q: What makes flying a small drone outdoors difficult?
85687.e: Small drones are light. Strong wind can carry them away.
85687.m: Small drones are best flown when there is little wind.

85688.q: What do many drones have a camera for?
85688.e: With the camera you take pictures and films from the air.
85688.m: Many drones take photos from the air.

85689.q: What must you not do with a drone camera?
85689.e: Everyone has a right to privacy. You must not simply film strangers secretly.
85689.m: I do not secretly film anyone with a drone.

85690.q: What does the abbreviation AI stand for?
85690.e: AI means artificial intelligence. It refers to computers that solve tasks that would otherwise need thinking.
85690.m: AI is short for artificial intelligence.

85691.q: How does an AI learn to recognise cats in photos, for example?
a: With lots and lots of example pictures
85691.e: You show the AI lots and lots of pictures of cats and other animals. That way it learns what makes a cat.
85691.m: An AI learns from a great many examples.

85692.q: How can a phone with AI recognise who is allowed to unlock it?
85692.e: The camera looks at the face. An AI compares it with the saved face of the owner.
85692.m: Some phones use AI to recognise their owner's face.

85693.q: Does an AI have real feelings like a person?
a: Yes, if it runs for a long time
85693.e: An AI is a computer program. It can write about feelings, but it does not feel anything itself like a person.
85693.m: An AI is a program and not a living thing.

85694.q: What is an AI good at, for example?
85694.e: AI programs can translate texts from one language into another.
85694.m: An AI can help with translating.

85695.q: What is a program that you can write to as if it were a person called?
85695.e: A chatbot answers questions that you type in. Many chatbots use AI.
85695.m: A chatbot is a program that answers in a chat.

85696.q: What should you do when an AI gives you an important answer?
85696.e: An AI can be wrong. That is why you look it up in a book or ask an adult.
85696.m: I check important answers from an AI.

85698.q: Which details should you not give away to an AI in a chat?
85698.e: Personal data such as your address or password does not belong in a chat, not even with an AI.
85698.m: I do not give personal data to an AI either.

85699.q: What do some robot vacuum cleaners record about the flat while they drive?
85699.e: With sensors they measure the rooms and save a plan. That way they clean every spot bit by bit.
85699.m: Some robot vacuum cleaners remember a map of the flat.

85700.q: What does a voice assistant use to give its answer?
85700.e: The answer is played as a voice through the loudspeaker.
85700.m: A voice assistant answers through a loudspeaker.

85701.q: What is hidden inside a seed?
85701.e: Inside every seed there is an embryo, a tiny young plant. A new plant can grow from it.
85701.m: Every seed holds a little plant.

85702.q: What does a seed need most of all to start growing?
85702.e: A dry seed rests. Only when it gets water does it wake up and start to grow.
85702.m: Without water a seed stays at rest.

85703.q: Where do the seeds form in many plants?
85703.e: In many plants the seeds form in the fruit. The fruit protects the seeds until they are ripe.

85704.q: Which fruit with a seed inside grows on the oak tree?
85704.e: The fruit of the oak is called an acorn. A new oak tree can grow from an acorn.
85704.m: An oak tree can grow from an acorn.

85705.q: Where do you find the seeds in an apple?
85705.e: The core is in the middle of the apple. The brown apple pips sit inside it, and they are the seeds.
85705.m: Apple pips are the seeds of the apple.

85706.q: What is a dried bean that you put into the soil?
85706.e: A bean is a seed. If you put it in damp soil, a new bean plant grows from it.

85707.q: How many seeds are there in a cherry?
85707.e: A cherry has a hard stone inside. There is just one seed inside the stone.
85707.m: A cherry has only one seed in its stone.

85708.q: Where are the little seeds on a strawberry?
a: On the outside of the skin
85708.e: The little yellow dots on the outside of the strawberry are tiny fruits. Each one contains a seed.
85708.m: The strawberry carries its seeds on the outside.

85709.q: What protects a seed from the outside?
85709.e: A tough covering called the seed coat surrounds the seed. It protects it from drying out and from damage.
85709.m: The seed coat protects the seed.

85710.q: What do we call a very young plant that is just growing out of its seed?
85710.e: A young plant just after germinating is called a seedling. It is still small and delicate.
85710.m: A seedling is a very young plant.

85711.q: Which part usually comes out of the seed first when it germinates?
85711.e: Usually the first root pushes its way out of the seed first. This way the young plant can soon take up water.
85711.m: When a seed germinates, the root usually comes first.

85712.q: What does the stem of a bean seedling look like when it is just pushing up out of the soil?
85712.e: The bean seedling pushes through the soil with a bent stem. This protects its delicate tip.
85712.m: A bean seedling comes out of the soil bent like a hook.

85713.q: In which direction does the stem of a seedling grow?
85713.e: The stem grows upwards out of the soil. Up there it finds light.

85714.q: What do we call seedlings that you can eat, for example from mung beans?
85714.e: Young seedlings for eating are called sprouts. People often eat them in salads or in Asian dishes.

85715.q: Where does a seedling get its food at the very beginning?
a: From the store in the seed
85715.e: A food store is kept inside the seed. The seedling lives on it until it can make its own food.
85715.m: At first the seedling lives on the store in the seed.

85716.q: Roughly how long does it take for a bean to germinate in damp soil?
85716.e: In damp, warm soil a bean usually needs a few days to about a week to germinate.
85716.m: A bean germinates after a few days.

85717.q: What does a seedling have to push through to reach the light?
85717.e: The seed lies in the soil. The seedling pushes upwards through the soil until it reaches the light.
85717.m: The seedling pushes through the soil to the light.

85718.q: What are the very first leaves that come out of the seed called?
85718.e: The first leaves of a young plant are called seed leaves. They are already inside the seed.
85718.m: The first leaves are called seed leaves.

85719.q: How many seed leaves does a bean have?
85719.e: The bean is one of the plants with two seed leaves. You can see them clearly when it comes out of the soil.
85719.m: A bean has two seed leaves.

85720.q: How many seed leaves does a grain of maize have?
85720.e: Like grasses, maize is one of the plants with only one seed leaf.
85720.m: Maize has only one seed leaf.

85721.q: Which seeds can you let sprout so that two large seed leaves come out of the shell?
85721.e: The sunflower has two seed leaves. Maize, wheat and rice belong to the grasses and have only one.
85721.m: Sunflower seedlings have two seed leaves.

85722.q: Do the seed leaves look exactly the same as the later leaves?
85722.e: Seed leaves are often simpler and rounder. The later leaves have the typical shape of the plant.
85722.m: Seed leaves often look different from the later leaves.

85723.q: What usually happens to the seed leaves when the plant gets bigger?
85723.e: Once the proper leaves have grown, the plant no longer needs the seed leaves. They wilt and fall off.

85724.q: Which leaves grow after the seed leaves?
85724.e: After the seed leaves, the plant grows its proper leaves. These are called foliage leaves.
85724.m: Foliage leaves come after the seed leaves.

85725.q: What colour do the seed leaves of cress turn when they grow in the light?
85725.e: In the light, the seed leaves make a green pigment. That is why the little cress leaves are green.
85725.m: In the light, seed leaves turn green.

85726.q: What can you sow cress on if you have no soil?
85726.e: Cress also grows on damp cotton wool or damp kitchen paper. The important thing is that it never dries out.
85726.m: Cress even grows on damp cotton wool.

85727.q: Roughly how quickly does cress germinate?
85727.e: Cress germinates very quickly. After just two to three days you can see the first little seedlings.

85728.q: After about how long can you harvest cress?
85728.e: Cress is big enough to harvest after about a week to ten days.
85728.m: You can harvest cress after about a week.

85729.q: How do people often eat cress?
a: As a dessert with ice cream
Cooked as a soup with sugar
85729.e: People like to sprinkle fresh cress on bread and butter, on eggs or in salads.
85729.m: Cress tastes good on bread and butter.

85730.q: What is the best tool for harvesting cress?
85730.e: You cut the cress with scissors just above the cotton wool or soil.

85731.q: Which parts of cress do you eat?
a: The young stems and little leaves
85731.e: You eat the tender stems with the little leaves. The roots stay in the cotton wool.
85731.m: You eat the stems and little leaves of cress.

85732.q: Can you grow cress indoors in winter too?
a: Yes, but only in the fridge
85732.e: Cress grows all year round in a warm home, for example on the windowsill.
85732.m: You can grow cress indoors all year round.

85733.q: What do you have to do every day with cress on cotton wool?
a: Let the cotton wool dry out
85733.e: The little seedlings dry out quickly. That is why the cotton wool must always stay damp.
85733.m: The cotton wool for cress must always be damp.

85734.q: What does a plant need light for?
85734.e: With the help of light, the plant makes its own food in its green leaves.
85734.m: Light helps the plant make food.

85735.q: Which way do plants on a windowsill grow?
85735.e: Plants grow in the direction the light comes from. That is why they lean towards the window.

85736.q: Where do plants outdoors get their light from?
85736.e: Outdoors, the sun provides the light for the plants.

85737.q: Where is the best place to put a houseplant?
85737.e: By the window the plant gets enough daylight. This helps it to grow well.
85737.m: Houseplants like to be near the window.

85738.q: Why do people turn a pot plant on the windowsill now and then?
a: So that it loses its fruit
85738.e: The plant leans towards the light. If you turn it now and then, it grows evenly and straight.
85738.m: A plant that is turned grows straight.

85739.q: Which plants grow well in the shade of the forest?
85739.e: Ferns need less light and like to grow in the shady, damp forest.

85740.q: Why do many woodland flowers such as the wood anemone flower as early as spring?
a: Because the trees have no leaves yet
Because it is darker in spring
Because there are no animals then
Because it snows the most in spring
85740.e: In spring the deciduous trees have no leaves yet. So lots of light falls on the forest floor.
85740.m: Woodland flowers use the spring light before the leaves come.

85741.q: What does a tomato plant need so that its fruit becomes ripe and red?
85741.e: Tomatoes love a sunny, warm spot. There their fruit ripens well.

85742.q: Which tall plant grows on the shores of lakes and stands in the water?
85742.e: Reeds grow on the shores of lakes and ponds. Their roots stand in wet ground or in the water.
85742.m: Reeds grow in the water on lake shores.

85743.q: How does water get from the root to the leaves?
85743.e: There are fine tubes in the stem. Water rises through them right up into the leaves.
85743.m: Water rises up through the stem.

85744.q: What happens to a plant that gets far too little water?
85744.e: Without enough water, the leaves and stems go limp. The plant droops and wilts.

85745.q: Which plant can go for a very long time without rain?
85745.e: Cacti often live in dry regions. They can store water for a long time.
85745.m: Cacti can survive long dry spells.

85746.q: Where does the water lily grow?
85746.e: The water lily has its roots in the bottom of ponds and lakes. Its leaves float on the water.
85746.m: The water lily lives in water.

85747.q: What can a droopy cut flower do if you put it in fresh water?
a: Grow new roots in a minute
85747.e: If a droopy flower gets water in time, its cells fill up again. Then it often stands up straight again.
85747.m: Fresh water can make a droopy flower stand up again.

85748.q: What is a cucumber mostly made of?
85748.e: A cucumber is well over nine tenths water. That is why it is so juicy.
85748.m: A cucumber is almost all water.

85749.q: Why does a flowerpot have a hole in the bottom?
a: So that extra water can drain away
So that air can blow in
So that worms can get in
So that you can hang it up
85749.e: Extra water drains away through the hole. This way the roots do not stand in water all the time.
85749.m: The hole in the pot lets extra water drain away.

85750.q: Why do people put a saucer under a flowerpot?
a: To catch water that runs out
85750.e: The saucer catches the water that runs out of the bottom of the pot. This keeps the windowsill dry.

85751.q: What are classic reddish-brown flowerpots made of?
85751.e: The well-known reddish-brown flowerpots are made of fired clay, known as terracotta.
85751.m: Classic flowerpots are made of clay.

85752.q: What do people often put in the very bottom of a flowerpot so that water drains well?
a: Gravel or bits of broken pot
85752.e: A layer of gravel or bits of broken clay pot over the hole helps the water drain away well.
85752.m: Gravel in the pot helps the water drain away.

85753.q: What do you do when a plant has grown too big for its pot?
a: You cut off all the roots
You put it in the fridge
85753.e: You put the plant in a bigger pot with fresh soil. This is called repotting.
85753.m: A plant that is too big gets a bigger pot.

85754.q: What is in good potting compost that feeds the plant?
85754.e: Good potting compost contains nutrients. The plant takes them up with water through its roots.
85754.m: Good soil contains nutrients for the plant.

85755.q: Which animal makes garden soil loose and fertile?
85755.e: Earthworms dig tunnels and eat plant remains. This makes the soil loose and fertile.

a: Soil made from rotted plant remains
85756.e: Over time, vegetable peelings, leaves and grass cuttings turn into dark compost that is rich in nutrients.
85756.m: Compost comes from rotted plant remains.

85757.q: What do you use to water flowers?
85757.e: With a watering can you can get the water exactly where the plant needs it.
85757.m: You water flowers with a watering can.

85758.q: When is the best time to water the garden in summer?
85758.e: Early in the morning it is still cool. The water can soak into the ground before the sun evaporates it.
85758.m: In summer it is best to water early in the morning.

85759.q: Why should you not water in the midday heat in summer?
a: Because lots of water evaporates quickly
Because water is poisonous at midday
85759.e: In the midday heat, lots of water evaporates before it reaches the roots.
85759.m: At midday watering water evaporates quickly.

85760.q: How can you tell whether a pot plant needs water?
85760.e: You push a finger into the soil. If it is dry, the plant needs water.
85760.m: Dry soil shows that the plant needs water.

85761.q: What can happen if you water a pot plant far too often?
a: The plant grows bigger than a tree
85761.e: If the soil is always waterlogged, the roots get no air. They can rot.
85761.m: Too much water makes roots rot.

85762.q: Where is the best place to pour the water?
a: On the soil by the roots
Next to the pot on the floor
85762.e: The plant takes up water through its roots. That is why you water the soil.
85762.m: You water the soil, near the roots.

85763.q: Which water is good for watering and costs nothing?
85763.e: You can collect rainwater in a water butt. It is soft and good for plants.

85764.q: What is the attachment with lots of little holes on the front of a watering can called?
85764.e: The rose spreads the water into lots of fine jets. This way delicate plants are not washed away.
85764.m: The rose spreads the water finely.

85765.q: In winter, do you usually water houseplants more often or less often?
85765.e: In winter most houseplants grow more slowly. They need less water then.
85765.m: In winter you water houseplants less often.

85766.q: What things does a plant need to grow?
85766.e: Plants need light, water, warmth, air and nutrients from the soil.
85766.m: Plants need light, water and warmth.

85767.q: In which seasons do plants grow the most where we live?
85767.e: In spring and summer it is warm and bright. That is when plants in Switzerland grow the most.
85767.m: Plants grow the most in spring and summer.

85768.q: What does a plant form before a flower opens?
85768.e: First a closed bud grows. Later the flower opens out of it.
85768.m: The flower opens out of a bud.

85769.q: Which order is right when a flower grows?
85769.e: A seedling grows from the seed. It becomes a plant, and later the plant forms flowers.
85769.m: The seed becomes a seedling, then a plant with flowers.

85770.q: Which plant is one of the fastest-growing plants in the world?
85770.e: Some kinds of bamboo grow more than half a metre taller in a single day.

85771.q: What is a gardener doing when he puts seeds into the soil?
85771.e: Putting seeds into the soil is called sowing. Later you can harvest what has grown.
85771.m: Putting seeds into the soil is called sowing.

85772.q: Where does a stem mainly grow longer?
a: Right at the bottom by the ground
In the middle of the root
85772.e: Plants mainly grow longer at their tips. That is where new cells keep forming.
85772.m: A stem grows longer at its tip.

85773.q: Why do most plants where we live hardly grow in winter?
a: Because it is cold and there is little light
85773.e: In winter it is cold and the days are short. That is why many plants rest.

85774.q: What do we call a dandelion when it has a white, fluffy ball?
85774.e: When the dandelion has finished flowering, it forms a white ball of little parachutes. It is called a dandelion clock.
85774.m: The white ball of the dandelion is called a dandelion clock.

85775.q: What shape is a dandelion clock?
85775.e: The many little parachutes sit all around the flower head. Together they make a ball.
85775.m: A dandelion clock is perfectly round.

85776.q: What happens if you blow hard on a dandelion clock?
85776.e: The little parachutes are only loosely attached. When you blow, they come loose and fly away.
85776.m: When you blow, the little parachutes fly away.

85777.q: What hangs at the bottom of each little parachute of a dandelion clock?
a: A tiny fruit with a seed
85777.e: A tiny fruit with a seed hangs at the bottom of each parachute. A new dandelion can grow from it.
85777.m: A seed hangs from each little parachute.

85778.q: What colour was the flower before it became a dandelion clock?
85778.e: The dandelion has bright yellow flowers. Only when it has finished flowering does it turn into the white clock.
85778.m: Before the clock, the dandelion flowers yellow.

85779.q: What does a dandelion clock grow from?
a: From a flower that has finished blooming
85779.e: After flowering, the flower head closes. A few days later it opens again as a dandelion clock.
85779.m: The dandelion clock grows from a faded flower.

85780.q: When do you see especially many dandelion clocks in Swiss meadows?
85780.e: Dandelions flower mainly in April and May. Shortly afterwards, the meadows are full of dandelion clocks.
85780.m: You see dandelion clocks mainly in spring.

85781.q: What is left when all the little parachutes have flown away?
a: A bare stalk with a round little head
85781.e: When all the parachutes have gone, only the stalk with the bare flower base is left.
85781.m: Without its parachutes only a bare stalk is left.

85782.q: On which tree do the small round fruits hang from a wing-like leaf and glide away?
85782.e: The fruits of the lime tree hang from a narrow bract. It works like a wing and lets the fruits glide away in the wind.
85782.m: Lime fruits glide away on a wing-like leaf.

85783.q: In German-speaking countries, what do children call the maple fruits that they stick on their nose?
85783.e: You can split open a maple fruit and stick it on your nose. That is why children there call it a nose pincher (Nasenzwicker). In English they are often called helicopters.
85783.m: In German, maple fruits are called nose pinchers.

85784.q: Which tree sends white seed fluff flying through the air in early summer?
85784.e: Poplar seeds have fine white hairs. They fly through the air like cotton wool or snow.
85784.m: Poplar seeds fly with white fluff.

85785.q: Why are seeds that are spread by the wind usually very light?
a: So that the wind can carry them far
So that birds do not see them
So that they sink in water
So that they are hard to find
85785.e: The wind can easily lift light seeds and carry them far away.
85785.m: The wind carries light seeds far.

85786.q: Which tree with white bark spreads its small winged seeds with the wind?
85786.e: The birch makes lots of tiny fruits with little wings. The wind spreads them far and wide.
85786.m: The birch spreads its seeds with the wind.

85787.q: Why is it good when seeds land far away from the parent plant?
a: The young plants have more space and light
The seeds get bigger that way
The parent plant then grows faster
The wind gets stronger that way
85787.e: Right under the parent plant it is crowded and shady. Further away the young plants have more space.
85787.m: Further away young plants have more space.

85788.q: In which weather do light seeds fly the furthest?
85788.e: Dry seeds are light and fly well. The wind carries them far.
85788.m: In dry wind seeds fly far.

85789.q: Which prickly plant has seeds with soft hairy parachutes like the dandelion?
85789.e: Thistles make seeds with a parachute of hairs. The wind carries them away like parachutes.
85789.m: Thistle seeds also fly with little parachutes.

85790.q: Where are the winged seeds of the spruce?
85790.e: Spruce seeds ripen in the cones. When the cones open, the seeds glide away on their wing.
85790.m: Spruce seeds are in the cones.

85791.q: How do burdock burrs spread their seeds?
a: They hook onto the fur of animals
85791.e: Burrs have little hooks. With these they get caught in animals' fur and are carried far.

85792.q: Which plant has round fruit heads with lots of little hooks?
85792.e: Burdock has round, prickly fruit heads. Their little hooks catch on everything.
85792.m: Burdock has fruits with little hooks.

85793.q: Which invention was modelled on the burdock burr?
85793.e: An inventor looked closely at a burr and copied its little hooks. That is how Velcro was invented.

85794.q: Which country did the inventor of Velcro come from?
85794.e: Velcro was invented by the Swiss engineer George de Mestral. He had the idea after a walk with his dog.

85795.q: Where do burrs often get caught when you walk across a meadow?
85795.e: The little hooks easily get caught in fabric. That is why burrs often stick to socks and trousers.

85796.q: What often happens to a burr that an animal carries in its fur?
a: It stays in the fur for ever
The animal eats it straight away
It grows into a plant in the fur
85796.e: At some point the burr falls out of the fur or is brushed off. A new plant can then grow in the new place.
85796.m: Animals carry burrs to new places.

85797.q: Which pet often brings burrs home in its fur after a walk?
85797.e: Dogs run through meadows and bushes. Burrs get caught in their fur as they go.
85797.m: Dogs often carry burrs in their fur.

85798.q: Cleavers catch on clothes with lots of little hooks. What do many people therefore also call this plant?
85798.e: Cleavers are covered with fine little hooks. The plant sticks to clothes, which is why it is also called stickyweed.

85896.q: Where in the mouth are the incisors?
a: In the roof of the mouth
85896.e: The incisors are at the front in the middle, at the top and bottom. You see them first when someone laughs.
85896.m: The incisors are at the front of the mouth.

85897.q: What do you need your incisors for when eating?
85897.e: The incisors are thin and sharp like little knives. With them you bite off a piece of apple, for example.
85897.m: We bite off food with our incisors.

85898.q: What shape are the incisors at the front?
85898.e: At the front, the incisors narrow to a thin, straight edge. That way they can cut well.

85899.q: How many incisors does an adult have at the top and bottom altogether?
85899.e: There are four incisors at the top and four at the bottom too. Together that makes eight.

85900.q: Which teeth usually fall out first in children?
85900.e: Usually the two middle incisors at the bottom wobble first. This often happens at about 6 years old.
85900.m: Often the lower incisors fall out first.

85901.q: Which animal has incisors that keep growing all its life?
85901.e: Beavers are rodents. Their gnawing teeth keep on growing and are worn down by gnawing wood.
85901.m: A beaver’s gnawing teeth keep growing.

85902.q: Why should you not open bottles with your incisors?
85902.e: The incisors are thin and not made for such large forces. A corner can break off.
85902.m: Teeth are not a tool for opening things.

85903.q: How many roots does an incisor usually have?
85903.e: An incisor usually has a single root. It anchors the tooth in the jawbone.
85903.m: An incisor usually has one root.

a: Right at the back of the mouth
85904.e: The canines are at the corner of the row of teeth. They come straight after the incisors.
85904.m: The canines are next to the incisors.

85905.q: How many canines does a person have in their permanent teeth?
85905.e: There are two canines at the top and two at the bottom too. Together that makes four.

85906.q: What shape is a canine tooth?
85906.e: The canine narrows to a point at the top. With it you can hold on and tear well.

85907.q: What do you especially need your canines for?
85907.e: With the pointed canines you hold tough food. That way you can tear off a piece of bread crust, for example.

85908.q: What is the part of the canine that sits in the jaw called?
85908.e: The canine sits in the jaw with a long root. That is why it is very firmly anchored.
85908.m: The canine has a long root.

85909.q: Which animal has very big, long canine teeth?
85909.e: The tiger is a predator. It grabs its prey with its long canines.

85910.q: What is another name for the long canine teeth of dogs?
85910.e: The long canines of dogs and wolves are called fangs. They use them to grab hold.
85910.m: A dog’s long canines are called fangs.

85911.q: What are the upper canines also commonly called?
85911.e: The root of the upper canine reaches far up towards the eye. That is why it is also called an eye tooth.
85911.m: The upper canine is also called an eye tooth.

85912.q: Where in the mouth are the molars?
a: At the back on the sides
At the tip of the tongue
85912.e: The molars are at the back on the left and right, near the cheeks. They are also called back teeth.
85912.m: The molars are at the back by the cheeks.

85913.q: What do the molars do with food?
85913.e: The molars have a wide surface. On it, food is ground into small pieces like in a mill.

85914.q: What does the surface of a molar look like?
85914.e: The chewing surface of a molar is wide and has bumps and little grooves. That way it can break food up well.
85914.m: Molars have a wide chewing surface with bumps.

85915.q: Which permanent tooth comes through behind the milk teeth at about 6 years old?
85915.e: At about 6 years old, the first permanent molar grows behind the milk teeth. No milk tooth falls out to make room for it.
85915.m: The six-year molar comes at about 6 years old.

85916.q: What are the molars right at the back called, which often only come in adults?
85916.e: The wisdom teeth are the molars right at the back. They often only come at 17 or later, sometimes not at all.
85916.m: Wisdom teeth usually only come in adults.

85917.q: Where do bits of food easily get stuck on a molar?
a: In the grooves of the chewing surface
On the tip of the tongue
85917.e: Bits of food easily get stuck in the grooves of the chewing surfaces. That is why you have to brush well there.
85917.m: You have to brush the grooves of the molars well.

85918.q: Which teeth do you use to chew a hard nut into small pieces?
85918.e: The molars are wide and strong. With them you can break up hard things well.
85918.m: We chew hard food with our molars.

85919.q: What is another word for a molar?
85919.e: Because molars grind food like a mill, they are also called grinding teeth. The technical word is molar.
85919.m: A molar is also called a grinding tooth.

a: A milk tooth that will soon fall out
A new tooth in a baby
85920.e: A wobbly tooth is usually a milk tooth that has come loose. Soon it will fall out.
85920.m: A wobbly tooth will soon fall out.

85921.q: Why does a milk tooth come loose?
a: A permanent tooth pushes up from below
Because you drink too much water
Because your tongue pulls on it
85921.e: The permanent tooth is already growing under the milk tooth. It pushes up, and the root of the milk tooth dissolves.
85921.m: The new tooth pushes the milk tooth out.

85922.q: At what age do many children get their first wobbly tooth?
85922.e: For many children, losing their milk teeth starts at about 6 years old. For some it is a bit earlier, for others later.
85922.m: Losing milk teeth often starts at about 6 years old.

85923.q: What happens to the root of a milk tooth before it falls out?
a: It stays stuck in the jaw
It grows onto the new tooth
85923.e: The body slowly breaks down the root of the milk tooth. That is why a milk tooth that has fallen out is often just a small crown.
85923.m: The root of a milk tooth dissolves.

85924.q: What takes the place of a milk tooth that has fallen out?
85924.e: After it falls out, a permanent tooth grows there. It has to last a lifetime.
85924.m: After the milk tooth comes a permanent tooth.

85925.q: Roughly how long does it take until all the milk teeth have been replaced?
85925.e: Losing milk teeth starts at about 6 years old and lasts until about 12. The teeth fall out one by one.

85926.q: What should you do with a wobbly tooth that is still firmly in place?
a: Wait until it gets looser by itself
85926.e: A wobbly tooth usually falls out by itself when it is loose enough. Forcing it only hurts.
85926.m: A wobbly tooth falls out by itself.

85927.q: What do new permanent incisors often look like at the edge?
85927.e: New incisors often have a slightly jagged edge. Over time it becomes smooth from biting.
85927.m: New incisors often have a jagged edge.

85928.e: The tooth fairy is a made-up character from stories. Children look forward to her visit when a tooth falls out.
85928.m: The tooth fairy is a fairy-tale character.

85929.q: Where do children put their milk tooth for the tooth fairy?
85929.e: The milk tooth goes under the pillow at night. In the morning, there is often something else there.
85929.m: For the tooth fairy, the tooth goes under the pillow.

85930.q: What does the tooth fairy take away in the story?
85930.e: In the story, the tooth fairy collects the milk tooth. In return she leaves a little surprise.
85930.m: The tooth fairy collects the milk tooth.

85931.q: What does the tooth fairy often leave behind in the story?
85931.e: Often there is a coin or a small present under the pillow in the morning. That makes saying goodbye to the tooth easier.
85931.m: The tooth fairy often leaves a coin.

85932.q: Which animal collects the milk tooth in France and in French-speaking Switzerland?
85932.e: In French she is called ‘la petite souris’, the little mouse. There she brings the present instead of a fairy.
85932.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, a little mouse collects the tooth.

85933.q: When does the tooth fairy come in the story?
85933.e: The tooth fairy comes while the child is asleep. That is why nobody sees her.
85933.m: The tooth fairy comes at night.
